# Blockscout

- [Blockscout blockchain explorer documentation](https://docs.blockscout.com/index.md): Blockscout is an open-source blockchain explorer for inspecting EVM chains, with support for 1000+ L1s, L2s, L3s, optimistic rollups, and ZK rollups.
- [Using an Explorer](https://docs.blockscout.com/get-started/using-an-explorer.md): Use the Blockscout explorer to search blocks, transactions, addresses, and verified contracts, plus set up My Account and access API endpoints.
- [Integrating Blockscout into your Application](https://docs.blockscout.com/get-started/integrating-data.md): Integrate Blockscout into your app using the PRO API, SDK notifications, MCP server for AI agents, and Chainscout multi-chain data endpoints.
- [Running Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/get-started/running-blockscout.md): Run your own Blockscout explorer using Autoscout, Docker, Kubernetes, or manual deployment. Hosted EaaS options and ENV configuration guides included.
- [Migration Guide](https://docs.blockscout.com/get-started/migration-guide.md): Migrate from Etherscan or other block explorers to Blockscout: switch links, APIs, and integrations for developers, projects, and end users.
- [API Rate Limits](https://docs.blockscout.com/rate-limits.md): Rate limits, credit allowances, and per-endpoint credit costs for each Blockscout PRO API plan tier.
- [Blockscout UI Sections and Page Overviews](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews.md): Navigate Blockscout UI sections including the top menu, blocks, addresses, transactions, and token pages to explore EVM blockchain data effectively.
- [Block Explorer Glossary of Terms](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews/glossary-of-terms.md): Definitions of common block explorer terms used in Blockscout including address, block, gas, hash, nonce, validator, token, transaction, and wallet.
- [Main Menu: Network, Blockchain, and API Navigation](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews/top-menu.md): Overview of Blockscout v2 UI top menu items including network switcher, blockchain data (transactions, blocks, batches, L1/L2), and API access.
- [Address Page: EOA Fields, Tabs, and Metrics](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews/address-page.md): Explore the Blockscout address page for EOAs: balance, tokens, transactions, ENS names, tags, watchlist, multichain data, and activity analytics.
- [Blocks Page: Block Height, Gas, and Rewards](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews/blocks.md): Understand Blockscout block views including block height, timestamp, gas used, validator rewards, burnt fees, base fee, and included transactions.
- [Transaction Fields Reference: Hash, Gas, Logs, State](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews/transaction-fields.md): Reference guide to Blockscout transaction page fields including hash, status, gas, nonce, input data, token transfers, event logs, and state changes.
- [Transaction Types: Blob, Coin, Contract, and Token](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews/transaction-types.md): How Blockscout categorizes transactions including blob (EIP-4844), coin transfer, contract call, contract creation, token transfer, minting, and burning.
- [Beacon Chain Withdrawal Views in Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews/beacon-chain-withdrawal-views.md): See how Blockscout displays Ethereum beacon chain validator withdrawals on block and address pages, including index, validator index, amount, and recipient.
- [Token Info Sources: CoinGecko and Verified Owners](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/overviews/token-info.md): Learn where Blockscout token metadata comes from, how CoinGecko and manual owner submissions work, and how to fix incorrect token details.
- [My Account](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account.md): Sign in to Blockscout My Account to add watchlists, private tags, custom ABIs, verified addresses, and receive email notifications on activity.
- [Watchlist: Email Alerts for Address Activity](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account/watchlist.md): Add EOAs or contracts to your Blockscout watchlist and receive email notifications for native coin, ERC-20, ERC-721, and ERC-1155 token transfers.
- [Private tags](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account/private-tags.md): Create private address and transaction tags in Blockscout My Account to label wallets, contracts, and transactions for your view only.
- [Public Tags: Request and Report Address Labels](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account/public-tags.md): Request public tags for your project's contracts or report incorrect labels on Blockscout, improving address discoverability and search visibility.
- [API keys](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account/api-keys.md): Blockscout API keys have moved out of My Account. Get a universal Blockscout Pro API key at dev.blockscout.com for your explorer requests.
- [Custom ABI](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account/custom-abi.md): Add a Custom ABI in Blockscout My Account to debug, test, and use the Write Custom feature on both verified and unverified smart contracts.
- [Verified Addresses: Prove Smart Contract Ownership](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account/verified-addresses.md): Verify ownership of a deployed smart contract on Blockscout by signing a message, then manage token info, name tags, and address labels from your account.
- [Copy and Sign Message for Address Verification](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account/verified-addresses/copy-and-sign-message.md): Steps for copying and signing the ownership message required to verify a smart contract address on Blockscout using your deployer wallet.
- [My Account setup for chain operators](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/my-account/for-developers.md): Developer notes for enabling the My Account feature on a self-hosted Blockscout instance, including env variables and Airtable integration.
- [Dappscout Apps Marketplace](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/blockscout-apps.md): Dappscout is a curated in-explorer marketplace of embedded dapps letting users connect a wallet once and interact across supported chains.
- [DApp Integration](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/blockscout-apps/dapp-integration.md): Integrate your dapp with Dappscout using iframe support and the Safe Apps SDK to gain top listing, embed inside Blockscout, and share wallets.
- [Widgets: 3rd-Party Data on Address and Contract Pages](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/widgets.md): Blockscout widgets surface reputation, airdrop, security, audit, and complexity data from partners like Talent Protocol, Webacy, Trustblock, and more.
- [Swap](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/essential-dapps/swap.md): Swap and bridge tokens across 18 EVM chains directly inside Blockscout using the LI.FI-powered Essential Dapp and earn Merits for activity.
- [Revoke](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/essential-dapps/revoke.md): Use the Blockscout Revoke Essential Dapp to review and revoke ERC-20 and NFT token approvals across Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Gnosis, Base, and Ink.
- [Multisend](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/essential-dapps/multisend.md): Use the Blockscout Multisend Essential Dapp to batch-send ERC-20 tokens to many addresses from a CSV list for airdrops and payroll.
- [Merits](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/merits.md): Blockscout Merits are cross-chain digital rewards earned by using the block explorer. Sign up, connect a wallet, and start collecting Merits.
- [Streak Rewards](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/merits/streak-rewards.md): Claim Blockscout Merits every day to build a streak and earn bonus rewards every 7 consecutive days, with up to 30 Merits on streak days.
- [Activity Pass](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/merits/activity-pass.md): The Blockscout Activity Pass unlocks extra Merits for contract verification, dapp usage, and everyday explorer activity, with weekly ranks.
- [Leaderboard](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/merits/leaderboard.md): The Blockscout Merits leaderboard on the Merits hub ranks accounts by earned Merits each season, with address search and shared rankings.
- [Badges](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/merits/badges.md): Earn and mint Blockscout Scout Badge NFTs on Base by joining Blockscout campaigns, with Common to Legendary rarity tiers for participants.
- [Earn Merits when using Swap](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/merits/earn-merits-when-using-swap.md): Earn daily Blockscout Merits by swapping and bridging tokens with Swapscout, distributed automatically based on your fees and daily volume.
- [Merits FAQs](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/merits/faqs.md): Frequently asked questions about Blockscout Merits and Scout Badges, including daily claims, referral rewards, streaks, and supported chains.
- [CSV Exports](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/export-to-csv.md): Download address-level transactions, internal transactions, token transfers, and logs from a Blockscout explorer as CSV files for analysis.
- [Token Standards Supported by Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/token-support.md): Blockscout indexes and displays ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155, ERC-777, and ERC-4626 tokens with balances, transfers, and standard-specific views.
- [ERC-1155 Support: Multi-Token Indexing](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/token-support/erc-1155-support.md): How Blockscout recognizes ERC-1155 contracts and indexes fungible and non-fungible balances, parses batched transfers, and tracks minting events.
- [Adding and Updating Token Info on Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/token-info.md): Submit or update token name, logo, description, website, and socials on Blockscout using deployer verification, manual review, or expedited processing.
- [For Web3 Developers](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/for-web3-developers.md): Developer hub for building on Blockscout with links to APIs, contract verification tools, the SDK, Merits integration, and link replacement guides.
- [Link to Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/replace-links.md): Swap Etherscan and other block explorer links for Blockscout URLs across transactions, blocks, addresses, and tokens with simple URL replacement.
- [Blockscout APIs](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/apis-redirect.md): Entry point to Blockscout API documentation covering the REST API, JSON RPC endpoints, GraphQL queries, and WebSocket event subscriptions.
- [What is WaaS](https://docs.blockscout.com/guides/developer-support/waas.md): Blockscout Wallet as a Service (WaaS) delivers ready-made wallet infrastructure with email or passkey login, swap, on/off ramp, and gas sponsorship.
- [Integration Guide](https://docs.blockscout.com/guides/developer-support/wallet-as-a-service-waas/integration-guide.md): Install and integrate the Blockscout global wallet SDK into your dapp with npm, connect to Rootstock or other supported chains, and enable WaaS features.
- [Current Integrations](https://docs.blockscout.com/guides/developer-support/wallet-as-a-service-waas/integrations.md): Current Blockscout Wallet as a Service (WaaS) integrations, including the Rootstock Global Wallet and the Polygon Global Wallet for ecosystem users.
- [Smart Contract Verification](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification.md): Verify deployed smart contracts on Blockscout using source code, standard JSON input, Sourcify, Hardhat, Foundry, Remix, and other methods.
- [Verify contracts using the Blockscout UI](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/blockscout-ui.md): Verify Solidity and Vyper smart contracts directly from the Blockscout UI using seven input methods including flattened source, JSON, and Sourcify.
- [Verify contracts with the Hardhat plugin on Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/hardhat-verification-plugin.md): Verify smart contracts on Blockscout with the hardhat-verify plugin, including setup steps for Hardhat 3 native support and Hardhat 2 configuration.
- [Sourcify plugin for Hardhat](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/hardhat-verification-plugin/sourcify-plugin-for-hardhat.md): Submit deployed contract sources to Sourcify from your Hardhat project so Blockscout can display verified metadata alongside on-chain contracts.
- [Verify smart contracts with Foundry Forge](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/foundry-verification.md): Verify Solidity smart contracts on Blockscout directly from the Foundry toolchain using Forge's built-in verification support and CLI flags.
- [Verify contracts via Sourcify on Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/contracts-verification-via-sourcify.md): Verify smart contracts on Blockscout using the Sourcify verification option, matching metadata and source files against Sourcify's decentralized repo.
- [Verify contracts with the Remix IDE plugin](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/remix-verification.md): Verify smart contracts on Blockscout directly from Remix IDE using the built-in contract verification plugin available since Remix v0.56.0.
- [Verify contracts via thirdweb on Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/verification-via-thirdweb.md): Deploy prebuilt contracts across many chains with thirdweb and verify them on Blockscout using the Blockscout contract verification API.
- [Stylus Verification](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/stylus-verification.md): Verify Arbitrum Stylus smart contracts located in public GitHub repositories using the Blockscout verification API and Stylus verifier endpoint.
- [Interacting with Smart Contracts](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/interacting-with-smart-contracts.md): Read from and write to verified smart contracts directly in the Blockscout UI by connecting a web3 wallet like MetaMask to any supported chain.
- [Smart contract verification websocket events](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/verification/websocket-notifications.md): Subscribe to Blockscout websocket notifications for smart contract verification results and automated source lookup lifecycle events on V2 and legacy sockets.
- [MCP Server](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/mcp-server.md): Blockscout MCP server wraps the APIs to expose balances, tokens, NFTs, and contract metadata for AI agents, IDEs, and automation tools.
- [Blockscout SDK](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/blockscout-sdk.md): React SDK for integrating Blockscout transaction notifications and history into dApps with real-time updates and mobile-responsive design.
- [Chainscout Chains List](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/chainscout-chains-list.md): Chainscout is a JSON-based directory of EVM networks running Blockscout, including chain IDs and metadata contributed via pull requests.
- [Blockscout Software Licence](https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/blockscout-license.md): Overview of the source-available licence adopted in Blockscout v11.0.0, covering permitted use for self-hosted explorers, chains, and resellers.
- [Autoscout Explorer Launchpad](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/autoscout.md): Autoscout is Blockscout's self-serve launchpad to deploy a production-ready hosted block explorer for EVM chains and rollups in minutes.
- [Creating an Instance](https://docs.blockscout.com/using-blockscout/creating-an-instance.md): Step-by-step guide to configuring an Autoscout explorer instance with chain info, RPC, branding, indexer tuning, and rollup settings.
- [Blockscout architecture overview](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/information-and-settings.md): Explore Blockscout architecture and organization including indexer, web app, API modes, umbrella project layout, ShareLock, and EVM versions.
- [Separate Indexer, Web App, And API](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/information-and-settings/separate-indexer-web-app-and-api.md): Run Blockscout components independently using DISABLE_INDEXER, DISABLE_WEBAPP, and API method env variables to scale services separately.
- [Umbrella Project Organization](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/information-and-settings/umbrella-project.md): How the Blockscout Elixir umbrella project is organized into ethereum_jsonrpc, explorer, block_scout_web, and indexer OTP applications.
- [Indexer Architecture Overview](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/information-and-settings/indexer-architecture-overview.md): Overview of Blockscout indexer architecture: realtime and catchup indexers, secondary and on-demand fetchers, and chain-specific integrations.
- [ShareLock](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/information-and-settings/sharelock.md): Understand PostgreSQL ShareLock behavior in Blockscout and how consistent lock acquisition ordering with Ecto prevents database deadlocks.
- [EVM Version Information](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/information-and-settings/evm-version-information.md): Reference table of EVM hard forks (Prague, Cancun, Shanghai, London, Berlin, and more) with mainnet blocks, opcode changes, and EIPs.
- [Requirements](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/requirements.md): System, hardware, database, node tracing, and JSON-RPC client requirements for running a self-hosted Blockscout explorer instance.
- [General backend requirements and prerequisites](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/requirements/requirements.md): Software dependencies (Erlang, Elixir, PostgreSQL, Node.js, GCC, GMP, and more) required to install and run the Blockscout backend.
- [Backend/Frontend Compatibility Matrix](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/requirements/back-front-compatibility-matrix.md): Version compatibility matrix mapping Blockscout backend releases to supported frontend versions for self-hosted explorer deployments.
- [Hardware & Hosting Requirements](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/requirements/resource-requirements.md): Recommended CPU, RAM, disk, and AWS EC2/RDS PostgreSQL baseline sizing for hosting a Blockscout explorer with an EVM archive node backend.
- [Database Storage Requirements](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/requirements/database-storage-requirements.md): Estimated PostgreSQL storage sizes for indexing Ethereum mainnet, Sepolia, Gnosis, Chiado, and Ethereum Classic in a Blockscout explorer instance.
- [Client Setting Requirements](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/requirements/client-settings.md): Configure Blockscout for Geth, Erigon, Nethermind, Besu, Reth, RSKj, Lotus, and Anvil JSON-RPC clients with the right endpoints and flags.
- [Node Tracing / JSON RPC Requirements](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/requirements/node-tracing-json-rpc-requirements.md): Archive node JSON-RPC methods, tracing endpoints, pending transaction support, and rate limits Blockscout needs to fully index a chain.
- [L2 to L1 JSON-RPC method requests](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/requirements/l2-greater-than-l1-json-rpc-method-requests.md): Reference of L1 JSON-RPC methods and polling patterns Blockscout fetchers use for Arbitrum, Optimism, Scroll, Shibarium, zkSync, and Polygon zkEVM.
- [Blockscout Environment Variables Overview](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/env-variables.md): Reference for backend, frontend, and microservice environment variables used to configure a Blockscout explorer instance across chains and integrations.
- [Backend environment variables reference for Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/env-variables/backend-env-variables.md): Reference for common Blockscout backend environment variables covering database, indexer, JSON RPC, API, and sanitizer configuration options.
- [Backend ENVs for Chain-Specific Configuration](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/env-variables/backend-envs-chain-specific.md): Backend environment variables for configuring Blockscout per chain type, including CHAIN_TYPE settings for Ethereum, Polygon, rollups, and other networks.
- [Backend ENVs for Blockscout Integrations](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/env-variables/backend-envs-integrations.md): Environment variables for configuring Blockscout backend integrations with Rust microservices, external APIs, and third-party services via MICROSERVICE ENVs.
- [Frontend ENVs: Common](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/env-variables/frontend-common-envs.md): Overview of common Blockscout frontend environment variables used to customize explorer UI, features, and container runtime settings.
- [Frontend ENVs](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/env-variables/frontend-common-envs/envs.md): Complete reference of Blockscout frontend environment variables for app config, API, UI, features, marketplace, and rollup integrations.
- [Deprecated Frontend ENVs](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/env-variables/frontend-common-envs/deprecated-envs.md): Reference of deprecated Blockscout frontend environment variables, their replacements, defaults, and versions where each was removed.
- [Deprecated Backend ENVs](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/env-variables/deprecated-env-variables.md): Reference table of deprecated Blockscout backend environment variables with defaults, versions introduced, and the release each was removed.
- [Blockscout Deployment Methods and Options](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment.md): Deploy Blockscout with Autoscout, manual setup, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Kurtosis, Terraform, or Ansible, including microservices and frontend.
- [Manual Deployment Guide for Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/manual-deployment-guide.md): Manually deploy Blockscout backend, new frontend, and microservices on your own hardware or cloud VM with step-by-step Ubuntu and macOS instructions.
- [Manual Blockscout Setup on Ubuntu](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/manual-deployment-guide/ubuntu-setup.md): Install and run Blockscout backend, frontend, and PostgreSQL on Ubuntu with apt packages, Erlang, Elixir, and Node.js configuration steps.
- [Manual Blockscout Setup on macOS](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/manual-deployment-guide/macos-setup.md): Install and run Blockscout backend, frontend, and PostgreSQL on macOS using Homebrew, with step-by-step instructions for a working local explorer.
- [Docker Compose Deployment for Blockscout](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/docker-compose-deployment.md): Run a full Blockscout explorer locally with Docker Compose, including backend, frontend, database, and microservices for development and testing.
- [Kubernetes Deployment with Helm Charts](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/kubernetes-deployment.md): Deploy Blockscout explorer to a Kubernetes cluster using the official Helm charts for backend, frontend, PostgreSQL, and supporting microservices.
- [Deploy Blockscout on Rollup Chains](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/rollup-deployment.md): Deploy Blockscout as an L2 rollup explorer with environment variables and settings for Optimism, Arbitrum, zkSync, and other supported rollup stacks.
- [Deploy Blockscout for Cosmos-Based Chains](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/cosmos-based-chains.md): Use Blockscout as a block explorer for Cosmos-based chains through the Fair Math SHUTTLE proxy, which bridges EVM-style RPC requests over WebSocket and HTTP.
- [Deploy Blockscout on Avalanche L1 Chains](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/avalanche-chains.md): Deploy Blockscout as a built-in add-on with Ava Labs' avalanche-deploy Infrastructure as Code toolkit for Avalanche L1 blockchains and validators.
- [Upgrade Guide for Blockscout v7.0 and v8.0](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/upgrade-guide-v7-0.md): Step-by-step upgrade instructions for moving existing Blockscout deployments to major versions 7.0 and 8.0, including database migrations and env changes.
- [Blockscout Frontend Migration Overview](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/frontend-migration.md): Choose a migration path from the legacy Blockscout UI to the new React frontend using Docker Compose, separate services, or a customized backend setup.
- [All-in-One Docker Compose Frontend Migration](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/frontend-migration/all-in-one-container.md): Migrate to the new Blockscout frontend using the all-in-one docker-compose.yml file that runs backend, frontend, and services in a single stack.
- [Frontend Migration with Separate Frontend](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/frontend-migration/separate-frontend.md): Run the Blockscout frontend as a separate service using external-frontend.yml so you can customize the UI or host it independently from the backend.
- [Frontend Migration with Customized Backend](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/frontend-migration/customized-backend.md): Migrate to the new Blockscout frontend while keeping an externally hosted or customized backend using the external-backend.yml Docker Compose file.
- [NGINX Proxy Setup for Frontend Migration](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/frontend-migration/proxy-setup.md): Configure an NGINX reverse proxy to route API, socket, and sitemap paths to the Blockscout backend while serving the new frontend from the same domain.
- [Frontend Migration FAQs](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/frontend-migration/faqs.md): Answers to common questions about migrating from the legacy Blockscout UI to the new React frontend, including tutorials, troubleshooting, and support.
- [Manual Deployment: Backend and Legacy UI](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/manual-old-ui.md): Deploy the Blockscout backend with the deprecated legacy UI on hardware or cloud infrastructure. Use the newer Manual Deployment Guide when possible.
- [Clean a Previous Manual Blockscout Instance](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/manual-old-ui/check-your-manual-deployment-instance.md): Remove build artifacts, node modules, static assets, and PostgreSQL data from a previous manual Blockscout deployment before redeploying or upgrading.
- [Terraform Deployment for Polygon Supernets](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/terraform-deployment.md): Provision Blockscout infrastructure with Terraform configuration files tailored for Polygon supernets, including new VPC or existing VPC deployment options.
- [Ansible + Terraform Deployment Overview](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/overview.md): Overview of the Blockscout Ansible playbooks and Terraform modules used to provision and deploy a production blockchain explorer on AWS.
- [Ansible Deployment Prerequisites](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/prerequisites.md): Required software, AWS credentials, and Terraform/Ansible dependencies to run the Blockscout deployment playbooks from a jumpbox or local machine.
- [AWS Permissions and Settings for Blockscout Deploy](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/aws-permissions.md): AWS permissions, IAM keys, and resources created for Blockscout Terraform and Ansible deployments, including VPC, ALB, ASG, and CodeDeploy setup.
- [Creating an AWS Secret Access Key Pair for CLI](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/aws-permissions/creating-a-secret-key-pair.md): Create an AWS access key ID and secret access key from My Security Credentials so the AWS CLI can authenticate for Blockscout Terraform deployment.
- [Login with AWS CLI for Blockscout Terraform Deploy](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/aws-permissions/login-with-aws-cli.md): Authenticate the AWS CLI with aws configure for Blockscout Terraform deployment: enter access key, secret, region us-east-1, and JSON output.
- [Creating An AWS Certificate For SSL](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/aws-permissions/creating-an-aws-certificate-for-ssl.md): Request and validate a public AWS ACM certificate for SSL on Blockscout, then set the ARN in terraform.tfvars via alb_certificate_arn.
- [Manually Clean Terraform Instances on AWS](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/aws-permissions/manually-cleaning-terraform-related-instances.md): Manually remove leftover AWS resources when Terraform destroy fails during Blockscout Ansible deployment, including S3, DynamoDB, and EC2 cleanup.
- [Ansible Deployment Variables Reference](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/variables.md): Reference for infrastructure, Blockscout, and shared YAML variables required by the Ansible playbooks to configure a Blockscout explorer per chain.
- [Provision Blockscout Infrastructure on AWS](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/deploying-the-blockscout-infrastructure.md): Use Ansible and Terraform playbooks to provision AWS infrastructure (VPC, RDS, EC2, S3) required before deploying the Blockscout explorer application.
- [Deploy Blockscout Application with Ansible](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/deploying-blockscout.md): Step-by-step Ansible playbook instructions for deploying the Blockscout application to AWS after provisioning the infrastructure with Terraform.
- [Destroy Blockscout AWS Infrastructure](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/destroying-provisioned-infrastructure.md): Tear down provisioned AWS resources for a Blockscout Ansible deployment using Terraform destroy commands to safely remove VPC, EC2, and RDS assets.
- [Ansible Common Additional Tasks](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/ansible-deployment/common-additional-tasks.md): Optional Ansible tasks for Blockscout deployments including clearing Terraform cache, migrating the deployer machine, and other maintenance operations.

- [List transactions, internal transactions and token transfers matching the advanced filter criteria](https://docs.blockscout.com/api-reference/advanced-filters/list-transactions-internal-transactions-and-token-transfers-matching-the-advanced-filter-criteria.md): Returns a paginated, mixed list of activity — native value transfers, internal transactions and token transfers — filtered by transaction type, contract method, time window, address relations, value range and/or token contract. The response also echoes the resolved human-readable names of the method…
- [Export advanced-filter results as CSV](https://docs.blockscout.com/api-reference/advanced-filters/export-advanced-filter-results-as-csv.md): Streams the items matching the advanced filter criteria as a CSV file. When asynchronous CSV export is enabled on the deployment, returns `202 Accepted` with a `request_id` that can be polled via `/api/v2/csv-exports/{request_id}`; otherwise the CSV body is streamed inline.
- [List known contract methods](https://docs.blockscout.com/api-reference/advanced-filters/list-known-contract-methods.md): Returns a list of known contract methods. When the `q` parameter is provided, searches for a single method by its 4-byte selector or name. Without `q`, returns the default list of popular methods.
- [List batches.](https://docs.blockscout.com/api-reference/arbitrum/list-batches.md): Retrieves a paginated list of Arbitrum batches committed to the Parent chain.

By default, returns the most recently associated batch. When `type=all`, returns a paginated list of all batches referencing this data hash.
